thread.title: Grow Southeast Alabama highlights regional milestones in innovation, workforce, and economic development
thread.title_full: Grow Southeast Alabama highlights regional milestones in innovation, workforce, and economic development

author: Wiregrass Times
title: Grow Southeast Alabama highlights regional milestones in innovation, workforce, and economic development
text:
June 1 saw Grow Southeast Alabama release its latest newsletter, outlining significant developments across the region’s 11 counties, including new training facilities, business expansions, and community achievements.
The launch of FLIGHTWERX Phase 1 marked a major milestone for the Southeast Alabama region. The facility, designed to enhance unmanned aerial systems (UAS) skills for active-duty soldiers at Fort Rucker, activated its initial training and innovation space this spring. Phase 2 will expand FLIGHTWERX into a broader ecosystem supporting soldier innovation, defense industry growth, workforce development, research, commercialization, and community engagement. Brigadier General Ken Cole, Deputy Commanding General, US Army Aviation Center of Excellence, said, “The character of warfare is changing, and unmanned systems are now central to how we train, fight, and win. Facilities like FLIGHTWERX give our Soldiers hands-on access to emerging technologies while bringing together academia, industry, government, and the community. We are excited about this collaboration taking place right here in the Wiregrass.” Melody Lee, Executive Director of Grow Southeast Alabama, said, “FLIGHTWERX is a defining moment for our region. This initiative not only supports the mission at Fort Rucker, but it also solidifies its position as a national leader in UAS defense and innovation. We are creating a space where ideas turn into capability; where military, industry, STEM outreach and higher education come together to shape the future. This is how we propel Southeast Alabama forward for generations to come.”
The newsletter also reported on the awarding of $1,000 workforce development scholarships to students from each of the 11 counties, made possible by a $10,000 investment from Troy Bank & Trust. In Pike County, Southern Classic Food Group announced a $14.2 million expansion expected to create between 82 and 240 new jobs over the next two years. The expansion will convert warehouse space into production, add new filling lines, and upgrade packaging and infrastructure. The investment is driven by Trillium Foods, the Illinois-based parent company, as part of its North American growth strategy.
Covington County received a $440,220 state grant through Alabama’s Site Evaluation and Economic Development Strategy (SEEDS) program to develop a new 110-acre industrial site. The SEEDS program, created in 2023 as part of Governor Kay Ivey’s “Game Plan” economic development legislation, provides grants to local agencies to improve sites for business recruitment. Covington Electric Cooperative and the county provided matching funds and property options to secure the grant. Houston County secured $419,999 in state funding for industrial access road improvements supporting the $80 million expansion of the Cencora pharmaceutical distribution facility, which is expected to bring over 60 new jobs to the area.
The Wiregrass Innovation Center officially opened in downtown Dothan on May 4, with Governor Kay Ivey and other leaders attending the ribbon cutting. The $30 million, 45,000-square-foot facility focuses on agricultural technology, peanut science, and STEM education, and is anchored by HudsonAlpha Wiregrass. Sentinel AG, an agricultural technology company, has also established operations at the center. Grow Southeast Alabama now has office space in the facility, which Governor Ivey described as “a destination for innovators and a place for experiential learning, and the nerve center for economic development.”
Other highlights included the opening of the Center for Applied Technologies at Enterprise State Community College, the participation of GSEA leaders in Leadership Alabama Class XXXV, and Union Springs’ feature in the new novel “Judge Stone” by James Patterson and Viola Davis. The newsletter concluded with an invitation for community members to share announcements for future publications.
